subject: general
question:
In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select “No improvement”.

__Hardly we had arrived__ when the whirlwind took place.
solution:
The correct answer is- **Hardly had we arrived.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Some negative adverbial expressions follow the inversion of the verb:

 
 
• Hardly, scarcely, never, no sooner, seldom, rarely, etc.
 
 
 
• For example:
 
 
• Rarely we see gypsies*. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b91b169c9a6aba309887b5e1410c56688829831001bc1448ed23f1bec5eca1d8.png] *
 
• Rarely do we see gypsies*. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/69a779acc017790d2eea790cc9122762921b180090c4a6901b9133fe30db56bd.png] *
 
 
 
• According to the rule and the example given above, '**Hardly had we arrived**' will be used in the underlined part of the sentence.

 

Correct Sentence__:* **Hardly had we arrived** when the whirlwind took place.*

*​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__***

 
• ​​​​To add emphasis, 'not only' can be used at the beginning of a clause.
 
• When it is done, we invert the subject and the verb.
 
• Conditionals without the conjunction follow inversion of the verb.
 
• Example: 
 
 
• *Not only did she forget my birthday but she also didn’t apologize for forgetting it.*
 
• *Had he been there, he could have seen it.*
